ai.description: *Melanophidium khairei* is a slender, iridescent black shieldtail reaching 45 cm. It features a blunt, rounded head, a small terminal tail spine, and distinct white ventral spots.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Melanophidium khairei* is distinguished by its unique, distinctively pale or white-spotted ventral coloration, which contrasts sharply with the solid black belly of other *Melanophidium* species.
ai.habitat: *Melanophidium khairei* inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the northern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Khaire's Black Shieldtail is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its life burrowing through loose soil in search of earthworms and other soft-bodied prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Melanophidium khairei* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Melanophidium khairei is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, specifically occurring in the states of Goa, Karnataka, and Maharashtra at mid-to-high elevations.
